answer: Each agent earns a reputation token stamped with a unique umber‑colored hash that is tied to a quartz‑signed proof of computational work; the token is recorded in a distributed meadow ledger. When voting, the protocol applies quadratic weighting, so a single token contributes one vote while n tokens from distinct identities contribute only √n effective votes, dramatically diluting sybil clusters. An attacker must therefore invest enough real work to generate costly quartz proofs for each new identity, making a mass of fake agents economically prohibitive.
